Definition: properly, something expansive, i.e. a bag
BiblicalUsage: The word is a sack — the bag Joseph's brothers carried their grain in — and it shows up twelve times in the Joseph story, always at the same point: one brother opens his sack at the inn and finds his money in its mouth; Joseph orders the steward to fill the men's sacks with food and put every man's money in his sack's mouth; and in the last sack, Benjamin's, the silver cup is found. The sack is where the test happens.
TheologicalSignificance: A sack is only a bag, and it carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is Joseph's test — the money in the mouth of the sack, and the cup that proved his brothers' hearts.
